title: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi made the remarks in a documentary report to the public on August 18.
text:
Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi made the remarks in a documentary report to the public on August 18."

""
"- Abbas Araghchi, Iran's FM: "The perception of a weakened Iran has been decisively shattered. Prior to the war, a combination of regional developments, domestic events, including the December unrests and economic challenges had gradually fostered a global impression that Iran was vulnerable. It was precisely this miscalculation that invited aggression, as our adversaries believed they could dismantle a fragile Iran within a matter of days.""

"- Abbas Araghchi, Iran's FM: "Following 40 days of steadfast resistance, the narrative of a weak Iran has been replaced by the reality of a tough, resilient nation, one capable of standing firm under the most severe conditions.""

"- Abbas Araghchi, Iran's FM: "In the first two weeks of the conflict, the United States did not propose a ceasefire. Several other nations offered to mediate, but our response and the President's position, was unequivocal: we are not seeking a temporary pause; we seek a definitive end to the war. A 12-day war which was followed halt that merely postpones a renewed assault a few months later is unacceptable. We refuse to let this become a recurring cycle. That is why we oppose a ceasefire this time; the war must conclude in a manner that ensures it is never reignited.""

"- Abbas Araghchi, Iran's FM: "This war has fundamentally reshaped regional perceptions of the security architecture. In the past, there was heavy reliance on foreign forces to guarantee stability. However, the recent conflict has proven that foreign troops and bases do not enhance security, they destabilize it. In fact, countries without American bases on their soil emerged safer and less affected than those hosting such installations, which were supposed to be protected. Instead, the United States prioritized support for the Zionist regime and failed to shield its allies from strikes that, ironically, targeted American bases, assets, and interests within those very host nations.
